points.why: It notes that rising trust lowers scrutiny and detection, but never closes the loop back to trust or identifies it as reinforcing.
It argues clearly that 'no errors reported' reflects reduced detection, but never treats trust as a slowly draining stock.
It recommends random fixed sampling, risk-tiered gates on high-stakes clauses, citations to the source, seeded errors and re-escalation triggers.
It never raises whether lawyers, especially juniors, are losing the skill of reading contracts.

pitfalls.why: It calls reduced review reasonable if accuracy is measured, and judges the tool neither untrustworthy nor proven safe.
